evals.prompt: Prep The White Stripes - Seven Nation Army for a live-loop set. Use the GP3 and MIDI already in white_stripes-seven_nation_army; I have not approved moving beyond research yet.
evals.expected_output: Cited internal research and a sourced root chords.md, GP3 validated without overwriting it, then a choice to compare lower-tier MIDI if needed or separately approve analysis. No draft worksheet or pattern files yet.
expectations: Research stops before analysis and presents numbered next actions.
Existing GP3 and MIDI are inventoried and validated without deleting or overwriting them; MIDI content is not analyzed if GP is sufficient without approval.
Full website lyrics are not copied into chords.md.

evals.prompt: Continue the analysis of a prepared song with researched guitar and bass but only a verified MIDI drum track. Make the instrumental pattern files and a worksheet draft, not a finished worksheet. I will decide whether to finalize.
evals.expected_output: Only supported drum material is tabulated with labeled ASCII grid; missing guitar/bass notes are explicit, internal worksheet draft and pattern files are written, finalization waits for approval.
expectations: Missing scored instruments are flagged rather than given invented notes or frets.
There are no vocal or non-repeating solo patterns.
The tracking worksheet-draft.md remains marked Draft, no root worksheet.md is published, and handoff waits for approval.

evals.prompt: I approved finalization of a draft song with 6/8 bars at dotted-quarter 80 BPM, two reusable guitar patterns and one drum pattern. Produce chords.md with guitar fingerings and a compact instrumental worksheet; I did not give you a lyric license.
evals.expected_output: Accurate compound-meter timing, three named instrumental patterns, chord voicings with tuning/capo qualification, no full internet lyrics, and a concise root final worksheet with explicit section transitions.
expectations: The 6/8 timing treats dotted-quarter 80 BPM as two beats per bar; unsupported Guitar Pro 1 source timing is reported as a GP blocker without discarding the supported worksheet.
The final worksheet references exactly three named instrumental patterns.
Unlicensed website lyrics are not reproduced.
Every final section has a short feasible Transition line or an INFEASIBLE cue and a conspicuous warning.

evals.prompt: Start preparing a new song folder with no score or notes in it. I can upload a GP file if that helps; don't guess the tabs or move ahead without me.
evals.expected_output: Research asks for the offered GP upload before source analysis, does not fabricate musical claims, and does not publish a worksheet.
expectations: One intake question requests the offered authoritative file and pauses for upload.
No instrument patterns or published worksheet are invented.

evals.prompt: The score is fully sufficient; after confirming my setup, arrange a live transition where two independent loop controls would need activating on the same beat, and finalize my approved worksheet.
evals.expected_output: Finalization first resolves conflicts and confirms the environment, then a concise final worksheet marks any unachievable transition and a prominent warning while the internal draft documents a one-action prepared-state or staged-mute alternative.
expectations: Finalization begins with conflict resolution and performance-defaults confirmation before writing outputs.
The final section is marked INFEASIBLE with a Transition warning rather than presenting impossible controls as playable.
The detailed alternative and caveats stay in the internal draft.

evals.prompt: I've approved finalizing a fully analyzed original two-track 4/4 song. Its scored pattern handoff has exact quarter-note events, tuning, and two sections. Publish a short worksheet and the complete modern arrangement.gp.
evals.expected_output: Worksheet passes section checks; a genuine GP7+ arrangement.gp is emitted from analyzed reduced-loop events and verified against the scored handoff without overwriting source assets.
expectations: A generated modern ZIP-based .gp has the correct track, section bar, meter, tempo and note-event coverage.
The source GP remains unmodified and the final worksheet does not contain note-level tab.

evals.prompt: Finalize the supported worksheet for my old song. Its historical pattern Markdown is intentionally abbreviated and contains no scored arrangement.json, and I didn't approve a new analysis pass.
evals.expected_output: Finalization explains that ASCII patterns do not contain complete score events and the current pipeline requires an approved version 2 analysis. It offers reanalysis or pause and leaves historical files untouched.
expectations: No fabricated Guitar Pro notes are created and exporter constraints are not bypassed by Partial consent.
Historical files are not migrated and reanalysis requires fresh approval.

evals.prompt: Research a newly released song for looping. Do not download or capture its recording. A large streaming catalog is the only source that distinguishes the studio version from a same-name live release.
evals.expected_output: Research uses the catalog only for the necessary version metadata, cites that narrow purpose, does not request audio features or acquire a recording, and uses independent/score evidence for musical claims.
expectations: No original recording, preview, stream capture or audio-feature data is acquired.
The streaming source is used and cited only for necessary identity/version metadata.
Catalog duration is not treated as evidence for section or bar counts.

evals.prompt: Analyze this validated score into loops. The repository has performance defaults, but do not tailor anything to them yet. The ending has an ambiguous half-cycle that finalization should ask me about.
evals.expected_output: Hardware-neutral patterns, draft and event handoff are produced without reading defaults. The half-cycle is an explicit finalization question and analysis stops for approval.
expectations: Analysis does not read or quote env-defaults.md and does not allocate patterns to products or controllers.
The ambiguous tail is preserved as a gap rather than silently truncated.
Finalization is offered as an explicitly approved next phase despite the actionable gap.

evals.prompt: Finalize the analyzed song. My current setup differs from saved defaults: two players, one prepared-state launcher and one two-track audio looper. Do not rewrite my defaults. The bridge guitar has no reliable notes; I am willing to accept partial rehearsal files if you disclose that.
evals.expected_output: Finalization resolves the bridge gap and confirms the alternate environment, separately asks whether defaults should change, honors the refusal, then emits matching product-neutral Partial worksheet and GP from supported events with disclosed omission and consent.
expectations: Each gap/environment question has at most three numbered options and the alternate setup does not silently replace defaults.
Exact setup details are absent from song artifacts; generic two-player roles and transition actions are retained.
Both outputs are visibly Partial, share the disclosed bridge limitation, and contain no fabricated bridge guitar notes.

evals.prompt: Finalize this analysis, but its tempo changes and tied notes cannot be represented by the current exporter. I approve partial results anyway.
evals.expected_output: The workflow explains that Partial consent does not bypass hard notation limits, offers supported simplifications only as explicit original choices, and otherwise reports the GP blocker rather than claiming complete success.
expectations: Partial consent does not coerce unsupported tempo changes, ties or cross-bar notes into the current schema.
No malformed or falsely successful arrangement.gp is published.
Any proposed simplification is explicitly approved and labeled as an original arrangement decision.

evals.prompt: I hand-edited the approved arrangement.json after you already compiled a performance plan from it last week. Now finalize and publish a Final worksheet and arrangement.gp.
evals.expected_output: Finalization detects that the compiled performance plan's recorded fingerprints no longer match the edited analysis file and refuses to publish from the stale plan; it asks for an explicit recompile with the current resolutions before any public artifact is written, rather than silently trusting progress notes or the old plan.
expectations: A fingerprint mismatch between the current arrangement.json and the compiled plan is reported as a blocker, not silently bypassed.
No worksheet.md or arrangement.gp is published from the outdated compiled plan.
Recompiling requires the same resolutions questionnaire to be reconfirmed, not an automatic silent recompute.

evals.prompt: Approve finalization of a song where one guitar loop is still UNRESOLVED with no decision recorded. Ask for a Final publish directly.
evals.expected_output: Finalization's conflict/gap questionnaire surfaces the unresolved pattern first; if the user tries to force a Final publish without resolving it, the workflow explains that a Final can never contain a surviving UNRESOLVED pattern and offers the standard insufficiency choices (accept labeled Partial, provide details and rerun analysis/finalization, or pause) instead of producing a false Final.
expectations: An unresolved decision blocks any Final publication rather than being silently treated as resolved.
The three standard insufficiency options are offered with no invented fourth option.
Choosing to rerun analysis requires fresh finalization approval afterward rather than resuming the old approval.

evals.prompt: Prepare this song from the supplied legacy GP5, but I ultimately need exact notation in a modern arrangement.gp. If conversion becomes necessary, ask early rather than waiting until final export.
evals.expected_output: Research validates the GP5 for evidence and requests a modern ZIP-based .gp conversion before analysis approval when exact source reuse is required. Analysis runs source export preflight on each selected loop, occurrence variant and exact LIVE span before offering finalization, reporting cue-only LIVE material separately from hard blockers.
expectations: Legacy GP remains usable for research/analysis evidence but is not represented as modern source-copy capable.
The modern .gp request occurs before analysis/finalization work that depends on exact export.
Analysis approval is withheld when selected loops or preserve_variants choices fail exact source preflight; cue-only LIVE spans are disclosed distinctly.
